text: What's the story behind this Bible? Hey everybody, I'm Dan Mlelen. I'm a scholar of the Bible and religion. And a recent
video I posted on YouTube had a thumbnail image that included this Bible. And somebody asked me what the story behind that Bible was. So, I
thought I would share a video talking a little bit about it. This is my family Bible from my mother's side. She just
gave it to me about a year ago. And this is a Bible that was published most likely in 1885 in California by Braftoft Publishing.
And this is in my family in part because I am related to Hugh Braftoft who was an attorney and a publisher who was the
president of Dow Jones and Company from 1928 until his death in 1933, which was the year my grandmother, his
greatgrandise, was born. And so, as you can see on the title page, this includes the revised New Testament, which is the
revised version of the New Testament, which was originally published in 1881.
And then later in 1885, the revised version of the Old Testament would be published. And in this edition of this
Bible, they place the King James version and the Revised Version in sidebyside columns. So, here's an example where you can see on the left the King James
version, on the right column the Revised Version. And this is a page where we see the first example in the canonical New
Testament of a verse just being omitted from the revised version. And this freaks a lot of people out when they first read it because they wonder why
Matthew 17 goes straight from verse 20 to verse 22 and they think that something nefarious is going on. And the reality is that one of the reasons for
the existence of the revised version is that a lot of scholarship had unearthed a lot of older manuscripts and had
determined that there were a number of passages that were in the King James version which was based on the textus receptus the traditional edition of the
Greek New Testament first published by Desidarius Arasmus were not original that we had manuscripts from earlier centuries that lacked those passages and
we could explain how those passages work their way into the manuscript. And so starting with the revised version and in
New Testaments that are published all the way down to today, there are a number of verses, usually around 16 of them, that are just entirely omitted.
They usually are included in footnotes where it'll say as it does in uh the column down the middle of this page
between the two columns that other ancient authorities include and then they will quote verse 21 of Matthew 17.
And this is a very ornately decorated Bible. As you can see, it looks really, really rare, but they're actually one of
the most common Bibles that are still around today from the 19th century because there were so many of them produced. And my friend Reed Moon
recently made a video where he pointed out that these are not incredibly rare and they're not incredibly valuable. But I don't have this Bible because of its
value. I have it because I'm holding on to it as the family Bible from my mother's line and I treat it with a
tremendous amount of respect. And in the middle we have a bunch of marriages and births and deaths and newspaper
clippings and invitations to uh funerals and things like that that start in like 1813 and go all the way down into the
early 20th century when they kind of ran out of room to continue to write these things in there. So, this is a family
Bible of mine that I think is really cool. And now you know a little bit more about it. Hope that was interesting.
Thanks for watching everybody. And the fit for this video has been Electra.
